newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN TAKES ONE-SHOT LEAD INTO THIRD ROUND OF U.S. OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN TAKES ONE-SHOT LEAD INTO THIRD ROUND OF U.S. OPEN.

text.p: Tom Lehman's lead survived the wait, and the British Open champion will carry a one-stroke lead into the third round of the U.S. Open golf championship on Saturday.

Lehman was on top of the leaderboard with a three-under-par total of 137 when play was halted Friday due to failing light with 45 players still on the Congressional Country Club course because of a mid-round delay due to the threat of lightning.
Mark McNulty of Zimbabwe stood at two-under through 14 holes when play concluded on Friday and had a chance to catch Lehman when he resumed his round on Saturday.
McNulty, however, promptly bogeyed the 15th upon his 7 a.m. return to Congressional and then bogeyed the 17th as well to finish a round of three-over 73 that left him even-par for the championship.
Lehman led 1994 Open champion Ernie Els of South Africa and 24-year-old U.S. tour member Stewart Cink by one stroke. Another shot away were Hal Sutton, Scott Hoch, Jeff Maggert and David Ogrin.

Ten players were bunched at one-over-par 141, four shots behind Lehman, including Masters champion Tiger Woods, who bounced back Friday with a 67, and Briton Colin Montgomerie, who followed his brilliant opening 65 with a stumbling 76.
Players within 10 shots of the lead made the cut for the final 36 holes, leaving 84 out of the original 156-man field.
Just missing the cut was twice Masters champion Bernhard Langer of Germany (73-75).
Other notables failing to qualify for the final 36 holes included Briton Ian Woosnam (76 74), two-time Open champion Curtis Strange (79 71) and Australian Greg Norman (75 79).
Because of the large field remaining and the delay caused by the completion of the second round, the players were going off in threesomes for the third round.
The first group -- Vijay Singh of Fiji, Fred Couples and Ben Crenshaw -- was sent right back onto the course to start the third round at 10:10 a.m. (1410 GMT).
Lehman, Els and Cink comprised the last threesome, scheduled to tee off at 2:40 p.m. (1840 GMT).
